title: Symphony No. 8 in C minor
hook: Written in the year the war turned, it mourns instead of celebrating, and ends in a whisper.

painting.title: The Apotheosis of War
painting.pairingNote: A pyramid of skulls outside a broken city wall, dedicated by the painter “to all great conquerors, past, present and to come”; like the symphony, it looks at the cost of war rather than its glory.

facts: Shostakovich wrote the symphony between 2 July and 9 September 1943, mostly at the Composers’ Union retreat at Ivanovo, north-east of Moscow. The Red Army had won at Stalingrad that winter and was now pushing west. A victory symphony was expected.

Instead he wrote an hour of music that is mostly grief and violence, and that ends very quietly. In public he summed up its idea as “life is beautiful”; his friend Isaak Glikman called it his most tragic work.

Evgeny Mravinsky, to whom it is dedicated, conducted the USSR State Symphony Orchestra in the first performances in Moscow on 3 and 4 November 1943. The response was cool. Officials missed a triumphant ending, it was attacked at a meeting of composers in 1944, and after the 1948 campaign against “formalism” it was in effect banned until 1956.
In the West it was briefly called the “Stalingrad” Symphony, a title Shostakovich never gave it.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a long lament and an outcry (I), a grotesque march (II), a machine (III), a funeral [[passacaglia|passacaglia]] (IV), a pastoral finale that fades into silence (V). The last three are played without a break.

movements.heading: Adagio – Allegro non troppo
movements.summary: The longest movement, more than a third of the symphony. It begins slowly, with long, searching melodies. Gradually it speeds up and breaks out into music of terrible violence. After the climax, a single cor anglais sings a long, lonely solo, and the movement ends almost in silence.

mainIdeas.name: The opening motto
mainIdeas.description: a jagged, loud rhythm in the low strings, answered by the violins.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a long, quiet violin melody over a limping, off-beat accompaniment.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a violin melody in five beats to the bar, over an uneven pulse.

stops.hear: Cellos and basses, loud, in a jagged, dotted rhythm; the violins answer, and the sound sinks to a hush
stops.happening: The opening [[motif|motif]], the seed of the whole symphony

stops.hear: The violins, quiet, in a long, searching melody over a halting accompaniment
A new violin melody with an uneven, five-beat step
The woodwinds break in; the pace quickens
Snare drum, timpani and trumpets join; the brass bellow Theme 2 over shrieking woodwind [[trill|trill]]s
Faster still: a brutal march, then a huge climax with long, swelling drum rolls
stops.happening: The climax; the opening motto returns at full force

stops.hear: Over trembling strings, a cor anglais sings a long, lonely solo
stops.happening: Like a voice after the catastrophe, almost a [[recitative|recitative]]

stops.label: Last 2 minutes
stops.hear: A trumpet recalls the opening motto; the strings return to Theme 1, softly
stops.happening: The [[coda|coda]]. Quiet, with a little consolation

notice: Listen to the cor anglais at ≈ 17:00. After ten minutes of noise, a single instrument carries the movement for several minutes.

movements.heading: Allegretto
movements.summary: A short, loud, swaggering march with an edge of mockery. Shostakovich called it “a march with elements of a scherzo”. The orchestra’s extremes, the shrill piccolo and the growling contrabassoon, are in the spotlight.

stops.hear: A loud, heavy, swaggering march tune; brass and shrill woodwinds jeer
A shrill piccolo, high above, plays a skipping, cheeky tune over a thin, crisp accompaniment
stops.happening: The middle section ([[trio|trio]]), in the orchestra’s highest register

stops.hear: The march returns, louder and denser, the lines piled on top of each other

stops.label: Last 30 seconds
stops.hear: A last crescendo, then an abrupt stop

movements.heading: Allegro non troppo
movements.summary: A [[toccata|toccata]]: one line of even, hammering notes that never stops, like a machine. Over it the orchestra shrieks and stamps. The conductor Kurt Sanderling, who knew Shostakovich, heard it as the crushing of the individual. It crashes straight into the next movement.

stops.hear: The violas, loud, hammer out even notes, all the same length; the other strings stab chords
The violins take over the hammering; a two-note wail cuts across
All the violins hammer together, then the woodwinds in [[unison|unison]]
A solo trumpet plays a brash, galloping tune over the snare drum and the strings
stops.happening: The middle section: a fanfare from a circus or a parade ground

stops.hear: The whole orchestra, drums and cymbals, louder and louder
stops.happening: The biggest climax in the symphony

stops.label: Last seconds
stops.hear: The climax does not end; it breaks straight into the Largo

notice: Follow the hammering notes. They hardly ever stop, and they never change their length.

movements.heading: Largo
movements.summary: A [[passacaglia|passacaglia]], a set of variations over a slow bass line repeated again and again. The bass line grows out of the opening of the symphony. After the explosion of the toccata, this is the stillness of mourning.

stops.hear: The whole orchestra, very loud, still carrying the weight of the toccata; then the sound collapses
stops.happening: The bass theme, stated at full force

stops.hear: Cellos and basses, quiet and slow, repeat the same long line
stops.happening: The [[ground-bass|ground bass]], which is heard eleven times

stops.hear: A horn sings a long, sad melody above the bass
stops.happening: A lament over the repeating line

stops.hear: Lonely solos high above: a piccolo, very high and thin, and a clarinet, over flutes fluttering in place

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: Very quiet; the music slips straight into the finale

notice: Listen for the slow bass line under everything. It never changes; only the music above it does.

movements.heading: Allegretto
movements.summary: C major arrives, but not as a victory. The finale is a pastoral, a gentle, rambling set of episodes. In the middle the violence of the first movement breaks in once more. Then the music thins out and ends in a long, soft major chord, with a question still hanging in the air.

stops.hear: A solo bassoon, quiet, plays a lilting tune; the violins take it up
stops.happening: The main theme, almost a country dance

stops.hear: A solo flute over plucked string chords that make three beats sound like two
The bassoon’s tune returns in the violins, then in the cellos
stops.happening: The main theme comes back, as in a [[rondo|rondo]]

stops.hear: The instruments enter one after another with the same tune
stops.happening: A [[fugato|fugato]]; the music begins to gather strength

stops.hear: A huge, crashing climax, the cry of the first movement once more
Quiet again; solo instruments recall earlier themes
The violins hold a soft C major chord; below it, the lower strings pluck a short three-note figure
stops.happening: The [[coda|coda]]. The figure is the beginning of a theme that never continues

stops.label: Last 30 seconds
stops.hear: The chord fades away

notice: The symphony ends in C major, but very softly. Compare it with the blazing end of the Seventh: one year later, Shostakovich gave his listeners no victory celebration.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Kirill Petrenko, chief conductor of the Berlin Philharmonic, conducted this performance on 13 November 2020, when Berlin’s concert halls were closed because of the pandemic. It was streamed live from the empty Philharmonie and released in 2023. Petrenko has called the symphony an “incredible psychological drama”.

threads.title: One seed
threads.body: Almost everything grows out of the opening bars: the passacaglia’s bass line comes from there, and the first movement’s cry returns in the finale.

threads.title: The war without victory
threads.body: The first movement’s violence, the march, the machine of the toccata: none of it leads to triumph. The answer is a lament, and a quiet C major.

threads.title: Single voices
threads.body: After each catastrophe a single instrument speaks: the cor anglais in the first movement, the horn and piccolo in the Largo, the bassoon at the start of the finale.
